answer: TEE attestation resists sybils: each identity must register a hardware-signed quote from a real trusted execution enclave. Like a comet tracing one verifiable path across the ledger, the quote proves the agent runs on genuine silicon rather than a herd of cheap containers. Forgery hits its nadir: one physical device yields one attestation group, so minting ten thousand fakes means buying ten thousand secure chips or breaking vendor keys. Each clone costs as much as a marble of silicon it pretends to own. Limits: supply-chain trust is inherited and virtual machines are excluded.
